title: Certain agreements to be in writing
summary: Certain agreements are subject to a writing and signature requirement. These include a special promise to answer for the debt or default of another person, certain agreements involving marriage, contracts for the sale of land or an interest in land, and agreements that are not to be performed within one year from the making of the agreement. The agreement or a memorandum or note of it must generally be in writing and signed by the party to be charged or an authorized person.

title: Formal requirements - statute of frauds - UCC 2-201
summary: A contract for the sale of goods for five hundred dollars or more is generally not enforceable unless there is a writing sufficient to indicate a contract for sale and signed by the party against whom enforcement is sought. The writing is not enforceable beyond the quantity of goods shown. Between merchants, a written confirmation received within a reasonable time can satisfy the writing requirement against the recipient unless written objection is given within ten days. Exceptions include specially manufactured goods, an admission that a contract was made, goods for which payment has been made and accepted, and goods which have been received and accepted.

title: Modification, rescission, and waiver - UCC 2-209
summary: An agreement modifying a sales contract needs no consideration to be binding. A signed agreement that excludes modification or rescission except by a signed writing generally cannot otherwise be modified or rescinded. If the contract as modified falls within the statute of frauds requirements of section 1302.04, those requirements must be satisfied. An ineffective attempted modification may in some circumstances operate as a waiver.

title: Effect of acceptance - notice of breach - UCC 2-607
summary: A buyer must pay at the contract rate for goods accepted. Acceptance generally precludes rejection of the accepted goods. Where tender has been accepted, the buyer must notify the seller of a breach within a reasonable time after discovering or when the buyer should have discovered the breach, or the buyer may be barred from a remedy. The buyer has the burden of establishing breach with respect to accepted goods.

title: Seller's remedies in general - UCC 2-703
summary: When a buyer wrongfully rejects or revokes acceptance of goods, fails to make a payment due on or before delivery, or repudiates the contract, the aggrieved seller may use statutory remedies. Depending on the circumstances, the seller may withhold delivery, stop delivery, resell the goods and recover damages, recover damages for non-acceptance, recover the price in a proper case, or cancel.

title: Action for the price - UCC 2-709
summary: When the buyer fails to pay the price as it becomes due, the seller may recover the price of goods accepted. The seller may also recover the price of conforming goods lost or damaged after the risk of loss passed to the buyer, and in certain circumstances goods identified to the contract that cannot reasonably be resold.

title: Buyer's remedies in general - UCC 2-711
summary: Where the seller fails to make delivery or repudiates, or where the buyer rightfully rejects or justifiably revokes acceptance, the buyer may cancel and may recover the price already paid. The buyer may also cover and seek damages or recover damages for non-delivery. In appropriate cases involving seller failure to deliver or repudiation, the buyer may recover identified goods or seek specific performance or replevin.
